mainTopic: Wine and vinegar as one kind or two, and how produce is acquired: pulling, measuring, and the סמטא.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question. רבנן call wine and vinegar 'one kind', but only for separating תרומה and מעשר, following רבי אילעא's rule that תרומה from worse produce for better produce still counts. For buying and selling, everyone agrees they are two kinds, because people want different things. A new משנה then teaches that produce is acquired by pulling (משיכה), not by measuring. It adds that a smart buyer rents the spot where the produce lies, and that flax must be carried, or detached if it is still growing. In the גמרא, רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן that measuring produce and setting it in a סמטא acquires it, but רבי זירא suggests this only means measuring into the buyer's basket. A second quote of רבי יוחנן shows that רבי זירא is right: in a סמטא, the basket acquires and the bare ground does not. The גמרא then works out where the משנה takes place. Using אביי and רבא's rule on where each kind of acquisition works, it explains that the pulling is from רשות הרבים into a סמטא, and that the renting line is about privately owned land. The amud ends just as a new teaching of רב and שמואל begins.

steps.title: The ברייתא: wine and vinegar, one kind or two?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבנן say wine and vinegar are one kind, and רבי says they are two kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wine and vinegar are one kind. רבי says: they are two kinds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to suggest that our משנה, which treats wine and vinegar as different in a sale, matches only רבי and not רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבנן hold that wine and vinegar are 'one kind', then selling vinegar when wine was promised should not be a real mismatch. Yet the משנה treats it as one. So it looks like the משנה follows רבי against the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The first, unnamed opinion here is רבנן. The גמרא will call it 'רבנן' in the next line.

phrases.english: Wine and vinegar are one kind.
Rabbi says: they are two kinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that seems to set the משנה against רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה about a sale of wine that turned out to be vinegar follows רבי and not רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבנן call wine and vinegar one kind.

steps.title: רבנן only meant one kind for תרומה and מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow רבנן too. Their 'one kind' ruling applies only to separating תרומה and מעשר, in line with רבי אילעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבנן. רבנן disagree with רבי only regarding מעשר and תרומה, and they follow the view of רבי אילעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רבנן's ruling to תרומה and מעשר. It then sets up a source, רבי אילעא, to explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'one kind' ruling does not say wine and vinegar are the same in every area. It only means you may separate תרומה from one on behalf of the other. That limit removes the clash with the משנה, which deals with a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to this point
And in line with רבי אילעא

steps.confusionAlert: רבנן never said wine and vinegar are identical for every purpose. Their ruling covers only תרומה and מעשר.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis –
phrases.notes: 'It' means our משנה about the sale.

phrases.english: the Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi
regarding tithe and terumah,
and in line with Rabbi Ila'a –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the apparent clash raised by the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבנן treat wine and vinegar as one kind for everything, including sales.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן treat them as one kind only for separating תרומה and מעשר.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: תרומה from worse produce for better produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא asks for the source that תרומה separated from poor produce on behalf of good produce still counts. He quotes a פסוק about bearing sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: From where do we know that if someone separates תרומה from bad produce for good produce, his תרומה counts? Because it says: 'And you shall bear no sin because of it, when you set apart its best from it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אילעא's teaching. It explains how רבנן can call vinegar, which is worse, and wine, which is better, one kind for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar is a lower-quality form of wine. Normally you should give תרומה from the best. רבי אילעא shows that giving from the worse still works after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: From the poor produce on behalf of the good produce
Literally 'its fat'; here it means 'its best part'

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ila'a said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה,
phrases.english: From where do we know that one who separates terumah from the poor for the good,
his terumah is terumah?
As it says: 'And you shall bear no sin because of it
when you set apart its best from it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the רבי אילעא teaching mentioned in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That תרומה from poor produce for good produce is valid.

steps.title: Why the פסוק proves the תרומה counts
steps.stepSummary: If the poor produce did not become holy, there would be no reason to speak of sin. So the תרומה must count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it does not become holy, why would there be a sin? From here we learn that one who separates תרומה from bad produce for good produce, his תרומה counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק teaches the rule. The fact that you 'bear sin' shows that the act worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק implies that giving from the worse produce is a sin. A sin only makes sense if something actually happened. If the separation simply failed, the person did nothing at all. So the poor produce really becomes תרומה, even though he acted wrongly.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy, here meaning it took effect as תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: תרומה from worse produce for better produce counts after the fact, though it is wrong to do. This is why רבנן can let vinegar and wine count as one kind for תרומה.

phrases.english: If it is not holy,
why would there be bearing of sin?

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה,
phrases.english: From here we learn that one who separates terumah from the poor for the good,
his terumah is terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ, נְשִׂיאוּת חֵטְא לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the logic of the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the poor produce really becomes תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'sin' in the פסוק implies that the act took effect.

steps.title: For buying and selling, everyone agrees they are two kinds
steps.stepSummary: For sales, even רבנן agree that wine and vinegar are different. Some buyers want wine and some want vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for buying and selling, everyone agrees. Some people want wine and not vinegar, and some want vinegar and not wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. In sales, wine and vinegar are different kinds by everyone's view, so the משנה fits רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in a sale is what the buyer actually wanted. Wine and vinegar serve different uses, so getting one instead of the other is a real mismatch. That is true even for רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It suits him, he prefers it

steps.whatToRemember: 'One kind' depends on the area of law. For תרומה, רבנן say wine and vinegar are one kind. For sales, everyone says they are two kinds, so the משנה fits all opinions.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key method of the גמרא: the same pair of items can count as one category for one law and two for another, depending on what that law cares about.

phrases.english: But regarding buying and selling –
everyone agrees that they are two kinds,
since there are some who prefer wine
and do not want vinegar,
and there are some who prefer vinegar
and do not want wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from step 2 by explaining why sales are different from תרומה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה can follow רבנן. For sales, everyone treats wine and vinegar as two kinds, because buyers' preferences differ.

steps.title: Pulling acquires produce, measuring does not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that pulling produce completes the sale, while measuring alone does not. A smart buyer rents the spot where the produce lies.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone sells produce to his friend and the buyer pulled it but did not measure it, he has bought it. If he measured it but did not pull it, he has not bought it. If the buyer is smart, he rents the place where the produce is sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with the basic rule: for produce, the act that counts is pulling, not measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Measuring only shows how much is being sold. It is not an act of taking. Pulling (משיכה) is a real act of acquisition, so it completes the sale even before the amount is measured. Renting the spot works because a person's own space can acquire things that sit in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling an item toward oneself, a way of acquiring movable goods
He measured (only fixes the amount; it does not acquire)
He rents their place, so his rented space acquires the produce for him

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who sells produce to his fellow,
if he pulled but did not measure, he has acquired.
If he measured but did not pull, he has not acquired.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה פִּיקֵּחַ – שׂוֹכֵר אֶת מְקוֹמָן.
phrases.english: If he is smart, he rents their place.
phrases.notes: This way the produce is now sitting in the buyer's own rented space, so it becomes his right away without pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on acts of acquisition. It does not continue the wine and vinegar discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For produce, משיכה acquires and measuring alone does not. Renting the produce's location also acquires it.

steps.title: Flax must be carried, or detached if still growing
steps.stepSummary: Flax is only acquired once it is carried from place to place. If it is still attached to the ground, detaching any amount acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who buys flax from his friend has not bought it until he moves it from one place to another. If it was still attached to the ground and he pulled up any amount, he has bought it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. Flax needs a stronger act, carrying it, unless it is still growing in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flax is the kind of item people normally lift and carry, so pulling is not enough. It must be moved from place to place. If the flax is still growing, uprooting even a little counts as an act of acquisition.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached to the ground, still growing
He detached any amount, even a little

steps.whatToRemember: Produce is acquired by pulling. Flax is acquired by carrying it, or by detaching even a little if it is still growing.

phrases.english: One who buys flax from his fellow
has not acquired it
until he moves it from place to place.
And if it was attached to the ground,
and he detached any amount, he has acquired.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה, about flax instead of produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flax requires moving it from place to place. If attached, detaching any amount acquires it.

steps.title: Produce measured and placed in an alley is acquired
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: if the seller measured the produce and set it down in a סמטא, the buyer acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If he measured the produce and put it down in a side alley, the buyer has acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבי יוחנן's ruling, which adds a case to the משנה: measuring plus placing the produce in a סמטא does acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said measuring alone does not acquire. Here, the produce was also placed in a סמטא, a side alley that is not fully public and where people may set down their things. In that setting the buyer acquires it even without pulling.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A side alley, not a main public street

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict the משנה's rule that measuring alone does not acquire. Here something more happened: the produce was set down in a סמטא.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מָדַד וְהִנִּיחַ עַל גַּבֵּי סִימְטָא, קָנָה.
phrases.english: If he measured and placed it in an alleyway, he has acquired.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the משנה's case of measuring by stating where measuring plus placing does acquire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measuring the produce and placing it in a סמטא acquires it for the buyer.

steps.title: Maybe it was only about measuring into the buyer's basket
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי whether he heard רבי יוחנן's ruling only about produce measured into the buyer's own basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: Maybe you, my teacher, only heard this ruling about someone who measures into the buyer's basket?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא questions the scope of רבי יוחנן's ruling. He suggests it may only apply when the produce went into the buyer's basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the produce went into the buyer's own basket, the basket acquires it for him. The location would then not matter. רבי זירא is challenging the idea that simply setting produce down in a סמטא is enough.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi:
Perhaps my teacher did not hear it
phrases.notes: Here 'רבי' is a polite way of talking to רבי אסי himself: 'you, my teacher.'

phrases.english: except about one who measures into his basket?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of רבי יוחנן's ruling as רבי אסי reported it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's report that measuring and placing in a סמטא acquires.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Perhaps רבי יוחנן only meant the case where the produce went into the buyer's basket, which acquires for him, and not the bare floor of the alley.

steps.title: Measuring into the buyer's basket is too obvious to need saying
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי rejects רבי זירא's suggestion: produce in the buyer's own basket is obviously his, so רבי יוחנן must have meant something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said to him: This scholar seems like someone who has not learned the teachings. If he measured into the buyer's basket, does that even need to be said?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי pushes back hard. He says רבי יוחנן would not bother to teach something as obvious as the basket case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that produce placed in the buyer's own basket belongs to the buyer. A ruling about that would teach nothing. So רבי יוחנן's ruling must be about produce set down on the ground of the סמטא itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it need to be said?

steps.whatToRemember: This is רבי אסי's view: the basket case is too obvious to need a ruling, so רבי יוחנן must mean produce set on the ground of the סמטא. In steps 14-15 the גמרא concludes that in a סמטא only the buyer's basket acquires, which supports רבי זירא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: a statement is never read as teaching something too obvious to need saying.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This one of the Sages seems
like people who have not studied the teaching.
If he measured into his basket,
does it need to be said?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's narrowing of the ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אסי rejects reading רבי יוחנן's ruling as limited to the buyer's basket. The גמרא later adopts that reading in steps 14-15.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The basket case is obvious and would not need a ruling, so רבי יוחנן must mean produce placed in the סמטא itself.

steps.title: Did רבי זירא accept רבי אסי's answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי זירא accepted רבי אסי's rejection or held on to his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי זירא accept this from רבי אסי, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי זירא agreed with רבי אסי, or kept his view that רבי יוחנן only meant produce put into the buyer's basket. This question sets up the proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי said that produce in the buyer's own basket is obviously his, so רבי יוחנן must have meant produce on the ground. Now we want to know if רבי זירא was convinced. The next steps will try to prove each side.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it from him (agreed with his answer)

phrases.english: Did he accept it from him,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי זירא, and "him" is רבי אסי, who just turned down רבי זירא's suggestion.

phrases.english: or did he not accept it from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַיבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ, אוֹ לָא קַיבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the argument between רבי זירא and רבי אסי ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי זירא gave up his view that רבי יוחנן was only talking about produce measured into the buyer's basket.

steps.title: Proof from a partners' courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי quotes רבי: partners acquire from each other in their shared courtyard. The גמרא suggests this means even when the item is on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי ינאי said in the name of רבי, in a courtyard owned by partners, they acquire from one another. Doesn't that mean even when the item is placed on the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that seems to support רבי אסי. In a shared courtyard, one partner can acquire from the other, apparently even when the item is just set on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partners' courtyard is like a סמטא, since both people have rights there. If placing an item on the ground there already works, then רבי אסי is right, and רבי זירא should have accepted his answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for a proof
What, is it not...? (suggesting a reading)

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rabbi Yannai said that Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: A courtyard of partners:
they acquire from one another.
What, is it not when it is on the ground?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer step 11 by supporting רבי אסי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אסי's view, that placing produce on the ground of a shared area acquires.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ינאי quoting רבי, that partners acquire from one another in a shared courtyard.

steps.title: No, it means into the buyer's basket
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the partners' case is about measuring into the buyer's basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about putting it into his basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns down the proof. The partners' teaching can be about putting the item into the buyer's basket, not onto the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the case can be explained as the basket, it tells us nothing about the ground. So it does not prove רבי אסי right.

phrases.english: No, it means into his basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the partners' courtyard.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the item was on the ground, but it could be in the buyer's basket.

steps.title: Logic supports רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב quotes רבי יוחנן: measuring and placing in a סמטא does not acquire. This clashes with רבי אסי's quote unless we split basket from ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense, since רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if he measured and put it in a סמטא, the buyer did not acquire it. The two quotes contradict each other! So must we not say: one is about measuring into his basket, and the other is about measuring onto the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now supports רבי זירא. It shows a second quote of רבי יוחנן that says the opposite of רבי אסי's quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי quoted רבי יוחנן saying a סמטא acquires, and רבי יעקב quoted him saying it does not. The only way both can be true is רבי זירא's distinction: into the basket acquires, onto the ground does not.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense: brings support for a view
A side alley, partly public and partly private
Here... there: splitting two sources into two cases

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule: in a סמטא, the sale is done only when the produce goes into the buyer's basket, not onto the ground.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
phrases.notes: "It" means רבי זירא's view, that only the buyer's basket works.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yaakov said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If he measured and placed it in an alley,
he did not acquire.
They contradict each other!
phrases.notes: This quote clashes with the one רבי אסי brought in step 8, where a סמטא does acquire.

phrases.english: Rather, do we not learn from this:
here, when he measures into his basket,
there, when he measures onto the ground?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for רבי אסי falls, this brings support for רבי זירא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's distinction between the basket and the ground.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יעקב's quote of רבי יוחנן, set against רבי אסי's quote.

steps.title: Yes, learn from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: the distinction between basket and ground is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the reasoning of the last step. רבי יוחנן's two quotes are about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs רבי זירא's view. In a סמטא, only putting the produce into the buyer's basket completes the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the גמרא agrees

steps.whatToRemember: In a סמטא, measuring into the buyer's basket acquires. Measuring onto the ground does not.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with the reasoning of step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's two rulings are split into two cases: the basket acquires, the ground does not. This supports רבי זירא.

steps.title: Another proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says measuring without pulling does not acquire. The גמרא suggests this is talking about a סמטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he measured but did not pull, he did not acquire. Isn't that talking about a סמטא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring more support for רבי זירא from the משנה. Measuring alone does not acquire, and maybe the case is in a סמטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is about a סמטא, then measuring onto the ground there does not acquire. That would match רבי זירא.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he measured but did not pull, he did not acquire.
What, is it not in an alley?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings more support for the same view as steps 14 and 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's view, that measuring onto the ground of a סמטא does not acquire.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that measuring without pulling does not acquire.

steps.title: No, it is in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the משנה is talking about רשות הרבים, not a סמטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns down the proof. The משנה could be talking about רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רשות הרבים, measuring onto the ground surely does not acquire. So the משנה would tell us nothing about a סמטא.

phrases.english: No, in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed a סמטא, but the case could be רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Pulling does not work in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the משנה says pulling acquires. But pulling does not work in רשות הרבים, so the משנה cannot be about there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the first part: if he pulled but did not measure, he acquired. But does pulling acquire in the public domain?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 17. The same משנה says pulling acquires, and that cannot be true in רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both parts of the משנה are about the same place. Pulling acquires in that place, so it cannot be רשות הרבים, where pulling does not work. That brings back the idea that the משנה is about a סמטא.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the first part of the source
Pulling, a way of acquiring movable items

phrases.english: If so, say the first clause:
If he pulled but did not measure, he acquired.
Does pulling in the public domain acquire?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה is talking about רשות הרבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part of the משנה says pulling acquires, but pulling does not work in רשות הרבים. So the משנה cannot be about there.

steps.title: אביי and רבא: where each kind of acquisition works
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא teach that מסירה works in public, משיכה only in a סמטא or a shared courtyard, and הגבהה everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אביי and רבא both said: handing over acquires in the public domain and in a courtyard that belongs to neither of them. Pulling acquires in an alley and in a courtyard that belongs to both of them. Lifting acquires anywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a teaching of אביי and רבא. It shows that pulling does not work in רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each way of acquiring works only in certain places. Pulling is limited to a סמטא or a courtyard both people share. So the משנה, where pulling works, must be about one of those places, not רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: Handing over (for example, passing an animal's reins)
A courtyard owned by both buyer and seller

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מסירה and משיכה. מסירה (handing over) works in רשות הרבים, but משיכה (pulling) does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for the laws of buying: which kind of acquisition works in which kind of place.

phrases.english: But don't Abaye and Rava both say:
handing over acquires in the public domain
and in a courtyard that belongs to neither of them;
pulling acquires in an alley
and in a courtyard that belongs to both of them;
and lifting acquires in every place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the challenge in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that pulling does not acquire in רשות הרבים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The joint teaching of אביי and רבא on where מסירה, משיכה and הגבהה each work.

steps.title: Pulling means pulling from the public road into an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: The 'pulling' in the משנה means pulling the produce out of רשות הרבים into a סמטא, where משיכה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'he pulled' that the משנה also teaches? It means he pulled it from the public domain into an alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18. The pulling in the משנה is not pulling inside the public road. It is pulling the produce out of the road and into an alleyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 taught that משיכה only works in a סמטא or a shared courtyard. So the גמרא says the buyer pulled the produce into a סמטא, and the acquisition happens there. This lets the משנה still be set in רשות הרבים without contradicting אביי and רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He pulled. Acquiring an item by drawing it toward yourself (מְשִׁיכָה).
A side alley next to the public road. It is not fully public, so משיכה works there.
The public domain, a main public road.

phrases.english: What is the 'he pulled' that is also taught?
phrases.notes: This refers to the first part of the משנה: if he pulled the produce, he acquires it.

phrases.english: From the public domain into an alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18, using the rule of אביי and רבא from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the pulling moves the produce out of the public road.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pulling in the משנה happens inside רשות הרבים, where it cannot work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pulling takes the produce from רשות הרבים into a סמטא, where משיכה acquires.

steps.title: Renting the spot makes no sense on a public road
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says a smart buyer rents the produce's spot. On a public road there is no owner to rent from.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part of the משנה: 'If he is smart, he rents their place.' But if this is on a public road, who could he rent it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the משנה is set in רשות הרבים. It points to the last line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting a spot only makes sense if someone owns it. A public road belongs to no one, so there is nobody to rent from. That suggests the משנה is not about רשות הרבים after all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. Introduces a problem that follows from the last answer.
The last part of a משנה.
He rents their place. The buyer rents the ground where the produce sits, so the ground acquires it for him.

phrases.english: If so, say the last part:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה פִּיקֵּחַ – שׂוֹכֵר אֶת מְקוֹמָן.
phrases.english: If he was smart, he rents their place.
phrases.notes: 'Their place' means the spot where the bought produce is lying.

phrases.english: But if it is in the public domain, from whom does he rent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the setting of רשות הרבים that steps 17 and 20 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה is talking about רשות הרבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Renting requires an owner. A public road has no owner, so the סיפא cannot be about רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The renting line is about a different, privately owned place
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא describes a separate case, where the produce sits on someone's property. There the buyer can rent the spot from the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: if the produce is on property that has an owner, a smart buyer rents its spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the last line of the משנה is not about the public road. It adds a new case, where the produce is on land that belongs to someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה changes setting in the middle. The first part, about pulling and measuring, is in רשות הרבים. The renting line is about רשות בעלים, where an owner exists, so renting from him makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. The גמרא is explaining how to read the text.
Property that belongs to an owner.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two settings. Pulling and measuring are in רשות הרבים, where pulling means into a סמטא. Renting the spot is about produce on someone's private property.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the whole משנה happens in one place. The גמרא splits it: the renting line is a new case on privately owned land.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
And if it is in a domain that has an owner,
phrases.notes: These words aren't in the משנה itself. The גמרא is filling them in to show which case the line is about.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה פִּיקֵּחַ – שׂוֹכֵר אֶת מְקוֹמָן.
phrases.english: If he was smart, he rents their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the סיפא is a separate case set on private property.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה, including the renting line, is set in רשות הרבים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The renting line refers to produce in רשות בעלים, where an owner can rent out the spot.

steps.title: Introducing a teaching from רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement that רב and שמואל both say about how acquisition works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only introduces who is speaking. It sets up a new teaching from רב and שמואל that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section on the משנה's setting is finished. The גמרא now turns to a new statement on how acquisition takes place, and both of these great אמוראים agree on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Two leading early אמוראים in Babylonia.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section after the discussion of the משנה's setting ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a shared ruling of רב and שמואל about acquisition. The ruling itself follows.
